subject: PulseHealth private offer — annualization + split-billing acceptance plan
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PulseHealth private offer — annualization + split-billing acceptance plan

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, PulseHealth wants to annualize the current monthly Marketplace commitment into a 12‑month private offer with an immediate capacity uplift (from 200k to 350k token units/month) and a request to split billing into two tranches (70% / 30%) aligned to your fiscal cadence.

High-level we can support this with the following approach:
- Convert the existing Marketplace listing to a private offer (AWS) and generate a single PO that legal signs; Redwood will accept a two‑invoice billing cadence tied to the PO (invoice A = 70% at start of term, invoice B = 30% at month 7).
- Add a 30% upfront credit to cover the initial uplift ramp over first 90 days (applies to the first invoice).
- Provide standard SOC2 and evidence pack for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send an updated private-offer PO draft and DocuSign link for PulseHealth procurement to sign.
2) Kimberly / Finance to confirm acceptance of two-tranche invoice workflow and update AR contact.
3) Marissa to coordinate the Marketplace private-offer activation with AWS once PO executes.

I’ve attached a stubbed PO draft for reference (PO_PulseHealth_AWS_Private_Offer.pdf). Let me know if Procurement needs a different split or proration model.

Best,
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplace & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pulsehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: PulseHealth private offer — annualization + split-billing acceptance plan

Hi Nikhil —

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Procurement:
- We need the two invoices to be on separate invoice numbers and shipped to our AP team (ap@pulsehealth.com). Can you confirm Redwood Finance will support two invoice numbers tied to one PO?
- For the SOC2 / compliance package, we need redacted evidence and the attestation (PDF). Could you attach the SOC2 report and a short runbook describing data residency controls?
- We may request an amendment if our CFO asks to move to 3 tranches; can you confirm the amendment path and any fees for mid-term split changes?

If those are OK we can circulate the PO for signature this week. Also copying Bob from AWS Marketplace to confirm private-offer activation steps on the marketplace side.

—Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Procurement
PulseHealth
emma.liu@pulsehealth.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pulsehealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseHealth private offer — annualization + split-billing acceptance plan

Emma —

We can support the two invoice numbers against a single PO (Finance will issue Invoice-1 and Invoice-2 with distinct invoice IDs and reference to the PO). No additional fees for switching to a 3-tranche schedule if requested within the first 30 days — we treat that as a billing amendment and will update the AR schedule (we will surface any pro‑rations if the change occurs after month 3).

Attachments included for Procurement:
- redwood_soc2_evidence_bundle.zip (redacted artifacts + attestation.pdf)
- PO_PulseHealth_AWS_Private_Offer.pdf (draft)

Marissa — please escalate to AWS Marketplace ops once PO is signed; Bob, when you get a moment can you confirm the private-offer activation lead time?

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pulsehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Bob Stokes <bob.stokes@awsmarketplace.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: PulseHealth private offer — annualization + split-billing acceptance plan

Emma / team —

Following up with the paperwork and next steps. I’ve sent the PO into DocuSign for signature: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/session/ABC123-pulse-ds

Summary of confirmeds:
- Redwood accepts two distinct invoices against one PO (Invoice-1 = 70% at effective date, Invoice-2 = 30% at month 7).
- No fee for moving to 3 tranches if requested within 30 days of execution; after 90 days normal pro‑rations apply.
- We will apply a promotional 30% credit to the first invoice to offset ramp usage.
- Attached is the SOC2 evidence bundle for Procurement (redwood_soc2_evidence_bundle.zip).

Marissa will kick off the Marketplace private-offer activation with AWS once we have the fully executed PO; Bob from AWS please confirm activation ETA (our typical path is 48–72 hours once private offer is accepted in the marketplace).

Action items:
- Emma / Procurement: execute DocuSign PO and provide AP contact for invoice submission (ap@pulsehealth.com if different).
- Marissa: schedule Marketplace activation and confirm staging window.
- Kimberly / Finance: prepare Invoice-1 and Invoice-2 templates and send ACH instructions.

Thanks — I’ll circle back once DocuSign returns the executed agreement.

Best,
Nikhil

Attachments referenced: PO_PulseHealth_AWS_Private_Offer.pdf (DocuSign), redwood_soc2_evidence_bundle.zip
